note: Re-judged 2026-11-03 by an independent auditor who authored none of 816ce1ce4c, 2cbd255ba4, 2e5c2d012a, d22b811ce4 or 1a2ccaeef8 (phase 5 of spec-filter-wire-0-umbrella, the per-peer text filter chain deleted). RFC 7947 Section 2.1 read: "The route server SHOULD forward UPDATE messages from its Loc-RIB or Loc-RIBs to its clients as determined by local policy." The moved unit TestRFC7947ClientPolicyControlsWire changed only the filter plumbing: The test filter is now an answerTransport behind filterTransportSeam, compiled by answerPolicy into a policychain library chain, so the verdict travels the real filter-update path (route.Input, rpc.FilterUpdateOutput decoded by the library chain) instead of the deleted policyFilterSeam that handed a PolicyResponse straight to the text chain; that is the production path every plugin filter now takes. The per-client verdict now keys on input.Peer, the destination the export run is for, and the per-client call count uses transport.callsFor; it still requires exactly one export-policy call per client per round, one UPDATE with the exact NLRI and ORIGIN 2 to the accepting client and only the exact withdrawal to the rejecting one, with the accepting client swapped between rounds, so a verdict shared or leaked between destinations goes red. Assertions unchanged; tag claims unchanged and no wider than the body. Ran the tagged units under ./le job run at HEAD (-tags ze_bgp, -v): PASS (scratch audit-p5-units-v.log). Verdict unchanged: enforced.
